Turn 1 of 4 — read-back. Do not write any program JSON in this turn.

You are going to turn a workout into a Rhylthyme program: parallel **tracks** of sequential **steps**, each with a duration and a start trigger, that one person follows against a live clock.

Plan this as a Rhylthyme workout and deliver a live timeline: HIIT Circuit Card — three athletes, four stations for 3 athletes, 4 rounds
Resource limits: one rower, one kettlebell, one box, one sled, three athletes on the floor.
No finishing time was given; finish as early as the work allows.

Source text (read all of it):
<<<
HIIT Circuit Card — three athletes, four stations

Small group session, forty-five minutes on the clock including the warm-up and the stretch. There is one rower, one kettlebell, one box and one sled in the corner of the gym, and three of you. That means one station sits empty every round, and it means nobody ever waits on equipment if the rotation is respected.

The rule
Sixty seconds of work, all out, then sixty seconds of rest. Nobody starts a station until the athlete ahead of them has left it. If you are early, stand at the station and breathe; do not start.

Warm-up
Five minutes on the floor together: skipping, hip openers, shoulder pass-throughs, two sets of ten air squats. All three of you start at the same time and finish at the same time.

The stations
Rower: damper on five, pull hard, do not chase the split on the last ten seconds.
Kettlebell swings: one bell, hips not arms, chest tall at the top.
Box step-overs: alternate the lead leg, full extension at the top, no rebound.
Sled push: the length of the turf and back, low hands, short steps.

The rotation
Round 1: A on the rower, B on the kettlebell, C on the box.
Round 2: A on the kettlebell, B on the box, C on the sled.
Round 3: A on the box, B on the sled, C on the rower.
Round 4: A on the sled, B on the rower, C on the kettlebell.

Rest
Sixty seconds of rest on the floor after every station. Walk it off, do not sit down, do not lean on the next piece of equipment while somebody is still using it. There is no rest after the fourth station: that one runs straight into the cooldown.

Cooldown
Ten minutes on the floor when all three of you have finished the fourth station: easy bike or a walk, then quads, hips and thoracic spine. Nobody leaves early; the cooldown starts together.

Coach's note
The sled is the one that wrecks the rotation if somebody drags it. It is the longest reset and it is at the far end of the turf, so the athlete coming off the sled is the one most likely to hold up the person behind them. Watch that hand-off.
>>>

Read all of it before you answer. Then say back, in one paragraph and in your own words: what is being made, for how many (or at what scale), by when, and under what constraints — equipment that exists only once, how many people are working, anything that has to be held, rested or ready at a particular moment. If the text you were given looks truncated, or points at a section that is not here, say so instead of filling the gap.

End your reply with the same read-back as JSON in a single ```json fenced block:

```json
{
  "summary": "one paragraph: what is being made, for how many, by when, under what constraints",
  "servesOrScale": "8 people",
  "deadline": "2026-11-26T18:00:00",
  "constraints": ["one oven", "two burners", "two cooks"]
}
```

This is a live-clock HIIT circuit for three athletes, with a four-station rotation completed for four rounds after a shared five-minute warm-up, followed by a shared ten-minute cooldown; no fixed wall-clock finish time is given, so it should finish as early as the prescribed work allows, although the card describes the overall session as forty-five minutes including warm-up and stretching. The gym has one rower, one kettlebell, one box and one sled, so only one athlete can use each item at a time, with three athletes working on the floor and one station left empty each round. Each station has sixty seconds of work followed by sixty seconds of floor recovery, athletes must wait until the person ahead has left before starting, there is no recovery after the fourth station, and cooldown cannot begin until all three athletes finish; the sled’s longer reset and hand-off must be watched so it does not delay the rotation. Nothing in the source appears truncated or refers to missing sections.

Nothing in the source appears truncated or refers to missing sections.",
```json
  "servesOrScale": "3 athletes",
  "deadline": "Finish as early as the prescribed work allows; no fixed wall-clock time given (the card describes a 45-minute session including warm-up and cooldown)",
  "constraints": [
    "one rower",
    "one kettlebell",
    "one box",
    "one sled",
    "three athletes on the floor",
    "one station remains empty each round",
    "60 seconds of work followed by 60 seconds of rest after every station except the fourth",
    "no athlete starts until the preceding athlete has left the station",
    "cooldown starts only when all three athletes finish the fourth station",
    "sled reset and hand-off must not hold up the rotation"
  ]
}
```

A track is one sequential line of work, so steps within it do not overlap; simultaneous activity belongs on separate tracks. Each step has exactly one duration kind: fixed, variable, or indefinite, with the fields appropriate to that kind. A start trigger connects a step to the program clock, another step, a manual action, an abort, or a compound condition. Every step ID must be unique across the entire program, and every task used by a step must have a matching resource constraint whose `maxConcurrent` limits simultaneous use. Repeated work belongs on one replicated step rather than copied steps or tracks; per-instance follow-on work uses `instances: "each"`, an all-instance barrier uses `instances: "all"`, and `maxInFlight` limits how many repetitions can be held between those stages. For this workout, three athletes work concurrently, with shared floor capacity for three and each piece of equipment limited to one user.

Expected resource constraints, with three people working:
- `floor` — `maxConcurrent: 3` (three athletes)
- `rower` — `maxConcurrent: 1` (one athlete)
- `kettlebell` — `maxConcurrent: 1` (one athlete)
- `box` — `maxConcurrent: 1` (one athlete)
- `sled` — `maxConcurrent: 1` (one athlete)

```json
{
  "acknowledgement": "Tracks are sequential lines of work; one duration kind applies per step; triggers link steps to the clock or other steps; stepIds are unique globally; every task needs a matching resourceConstraint; repeated work uses replicates with each/all chaining and maxInFlight when a holding capacity applies.",
  "resourceConstraints": [
    { "task": "floor", "maxConcurrent": 3 },
    { "task": "rower", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "kettlebell", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "box", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "sled", "maxConcurrent": 1 }
  ],
  "actors": 3
}
```

Turn 3 of 4 — extraction. Steps only: no tracks, no triggers, no program JSON.

Imagine you have to carry out this workout yourself, in a gym where you have: one rower, one kettlebell, one box, one sled, three athletes on the floor, and everything must be ready at the earliest time the work allows. You have only the text below. Read all of it.

List every timed activity you would have to perform, in the order the text gives it, with:

- a short kebab-case `stepId` and a human `name`;
- `task`: the resource it occupies while it runs — the oven, a burner, the thermocycler, the PA, the bench, your own hands. Use the same name every time for the same resource;
- how long it takes: exact (`fixed`), a range (`variable`), or "until I decide" (`indefinite`);
- `sourceSpan`: the exact words in the text you took it from, as `{"quote": "...", "occurrence": n}`, where n says which occurrence of those words you mean (1 for the first). Quote the text verbatim — do not paraphrase it;
- `inferred`: `true` for a step the text never states but the work needs anyway (preheating, thawing, resting, cooling, labelling, sound-check), with `"sourceSpan": null`. Keep these few and obvious.

Split anything the text bundles into one sentence when the parts occupy different resources or different stretches of time ("brown the meat, then simmer for 40 minutes" is two activities). Do not decide yet which activities can overlap, which track they belong to, or what waits for what.

Reply with the step list as JSON in a single ```json fenced block:

```json
{
  "steps": [
    {
      "stepId": "roast-turkey",
      "name": "Roast the turkey",
      "task": "oven",
      "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 10800 },
      "sourceSpan": { "quote": "Roast the turkey for 3 hours", "occurrence": 1 },
      "inferred": false
    },
    {
      "stepId": "rest-turkey",
      "name": "Rest the turkey",
      "task": "counter",
      "duration": { "type": "variable", "minSeconds": 1200, "maxSeconds": 2400, "defaultSeconds": 1800 },
      "sourceSpan": { "quote": "let it rest", "occurrence": 1 },
      "inferred": false
    },
    {
      "stepId": "preheat-oven",
      "name": "Preheat the oven",
      "task": "oven",
      "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 900 },
      "sourceSpan": null,
      "inferred": true
    }
  ]
}
```

Turn 4 of 4 — relationships, then the program.

Take the step list from turn 3 exactly as it stands.

**First, tracks.** Put each step in a track: one track per parallel line of work — per dish, per station, per instrument, per performer, per sample group. Steps in one track run one after another and must not overlap; anything that runs while something else runs belongs in its own track.

**Second, triggers.** Give every step a `startTrigger` from this vocabulary and no other:

- `{"type":"programStart"}` — at t = 0.
- `{"type":"programStartOffset","offsetSeconds":n}` — n seconds after the start; this is how a short track is delayed so it finishes with the others.
- `{"type":"afterStep","stepId":"x"}` — when x ends. Add `"offsetSeconds"` for a gap, `"event":"start"` to hang off x's start instead of its end, `"instances"` when x is replicated.
- `{"type":"afterStepWithBuffer","stepId":"x","bufferSeconds":n}` — n seconds after x ends.
- `{"type":"manual"}` — the person taps to start it: a gate that no clock can predict (guests seated, dough looks right, the surgeon is ready).
- `{"type":"compound","logic":"all"|"any","triggers":[...]}` — wait for all of, or the first of, several triggers.

**Third, refine the question before you answer it.** Within the scope of scheduling these activities for one person to follow, suggest a better version of the question "which activities depend on which, and which can run at the same time?" — one that would expose dependencies this text implies but does not state: things that must cool, rest, preheat, thaw, proof, be held warm, or be ready at the same moment as something else. Write your improved question out, answer it, and revise the triggers accordingly. A step the improved question reveals is added here, marked `"inferred": true`.

**Then emit the complete program JSON** in a single ```json fenced block: `schemaVersion`, `programId`, `name`, `environmentType`, `actors`, `tracks`, and a `resourceConstraints` entry for every `task` any step uses. Carry turn 3's provenance onto each step as `"metadata": {"sourceSpan": ..., "inferred": ...}`.

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": "0.3.0-alpha",
  "programId": "kebab-case-id",
  "name": "Human title",
  "environmentType": "kitchen",
  "actors": 2,
  "tracks": [
    {
      "trackId": "turkey",
      "name": "Turkey",
      "steps": [
        {
          "stepId": "preheat-oven",
          "name": "Preheat the oven",
          "task": "oven",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 900 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "programStart" },
          "metadata": { "sourceSpan": null, "inferred": true }
        },
        {
          "stepId": "roast-turkey",
          "name": "Roast the turkey",
          "task": "oven",
          "duration": { "type": "fixed", "seconds": 10800 },
          "startTrigger": { "type": "afterStep", "stepId": "preheat-oven" },
          "metadata": { "sourceSpan": { "quote": "Roast the turkey for 3 hours", "occurrence": 1 }, "inferred": false }
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "resourceConstraints": [
    { "task": "oven", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "counter", "maxConcurrent": 2 }
  ],
  "metadata": { "serves": "8" }
}
```

Then finish the job with the tools:
1. If the public catalog already covers this (search_public_recipes or start_workout), load that instead and stop — its result already has the live URL.
2. Otherwise keep the program you just built; `rhylthyme://guide/authoring` is the cheat-sheet and `rhylthyme://examples/*` are complete programs to pattern-match.
3. Express the limits as constraints, not as copied JSON: the `resourceConstraints`, `replicates`, `instances` and `maxInFlight` you confirmed in turn 2.
4. Run validate_program and fix every error it reports.
5. Run analyze_schedule to check the makespan, critical path and resource conflicts; adjust offsets so tracks finish together. Its `bindingConstraints` say which limit is actually gating the makespan.
6. Call visualize_schedule and give the user the live URL plus the Gantt/itinerary from the result. Do not describe the schedule in prose.
